name: Germany
summary: EU citizens only register their address. Germany has no investor or digital nomad visa. Non-EU nationals can apply for a residence permit as a freelancer or business founder (Section 21 AufenthG; economic interest and funding needed), for the EU Blue Card at EUR 50,700 a year, or for the Chancenkarte (job-seeker card, proof of about EUR 13,092 of funds). Living off your own means is possible only as a discretionary permit with no published threshold.
naturalisation: Five years of lawful residence (since the law in force from 27 June 2024; the 3-year fast track was reported abolished at the end of 2025 by one source only), German at B1, secure livelihood without social benefits, a naturalisation test and commitment to the free democratic order.
dual_citizenship_note: Since 27 June 2024 applicants no longer have to give up their previous citizenship; the other country's law must allow it.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EU citizens register their address (Anmeldung) within two weeks of moving in; no permit.
routes.requirements: Freizuegigkeitsgesetz/EU; non-workers need sufficient means and health insurance. Permanent residence after 5 years.

routes.name: Residence permit for other purposes (independent means, Section 7(1) sentence 3 AufenthG)
routes.limited_places: discretionary: no right to the permit
routes.summary: A discretionary residence permit for people who do not work and can pay their own way; no statutory income figure.
routes.requirements: Granted at the discretion of the immigration office for purposes not covered elsewhere; secure livelihood without public funds and health insurance. No published threshold or programme was found; US citizens can apply from inside Germany. Not verified on an official page.
routes.tax_note: Unlimited tax liability follows domicile or habitual abode.

routes.name: Self-employment / freelancer permit (Section 21 AufenthG)
routes.summary: Residence for founders and freelancers whose business serves an economic interest or regional need.
routes.requirements: Economic interest or regional need, positive economic effect, and own capital or a financing commitment; applicants over 45 need adequate pension provision; exceptions for German graduates, researchers and Blue Card holders. US and some other nationals can apply in Germany. No fixed minimum investment.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Germany and run the business
routes.tax_note: Freelance income taxed in Germany if resident.

routes.name: Chancenkarte (Opportunity Card, job-seeker)
routes.summary: Points-based permit of up to 12 months to look for work in Germany, with part-time work allowed.
routes.requirements: At least 6 points (qualification, experience, language, age) or a recognised qualification; proof of funds about EUR 1,091 a month (EUR 13,092 for a year) via blocked account or sponsor; part-time work up to 20 hours a week. Secondary sources.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Germany while holding the card

routes.name: EU Blue Card (work)
routes.requirements: 2026: gross annual salary EUR 50,700; EUR 45,934.20 for shortage occupations (STEM, health), recent graduates and some IT specialists. Degree recognised in Germany; job offer. Secondary source.

sources.title: EU Blue Card Germany 2026: salary thresholds, shortage occupations and new rules

open_questions: Official Federal Foreign Office / BAMF pages not retrieved; Blue Card, Chancenkarte and naturalisation details come from secondary sources.
Section 7 independent-means permit: no authoritative source on practice or amounts.
Section 21 self-employment: years to settlement permit (3 years shown from general knowledge, not sourced) and fees.
Whether the 3-year 'turbo' naturalisation has been abolished: single source.
No investor, digital nomad or passive-income programme exists; absence not proven by an official statement.
